BOTH OF YOU BEGIN WITH THREE COMPOSURE POINTS. A
MATCHING REPLY COSTS YOUR OPPONENT ONE POINT. A
WRONG REPLY OR A YIELDED EXCHANGE COSTS YOU ONE.
THE FIRST PERSON AT ZERO YIELDS THE AGREED TOPIC.

THERE IS NO TIME LIMIT. YOU CAN REVIEW YOUR
NOTEBOOK BEFORE CHOOSING A REPLY.

WHEN YOU READ OR HEAR A LINE, IT IS RECORDED. ITS
REPLY IS LEARNED SEPARATELY. PRACTICE AND THE
RECAP TEACH THE MATCHES YOU STILL NEED.

A LOSS KEEPS YOUR ITEMS, LEARNED REPLIES AND
PRACTICAL PROGRESS. REMATCHES STAY AVAILABLE. WIN
ALL FOUR CONTESTS BEFORE THE FINAL COMMITMENTS.

SKIPPING SPEECH, PAUSING, OPENING A MENU, SAVING
OR LOADING DOES NOT YIELD AN EXCHANGE. USE THE
LABELED YIELD OPTION IF YOU WANT TO CONCEDE.

PRACTICE IS UNSCORED. READ THE LINE AND ITS
MATCHING REPLY, THEN TRY THE EXCHANGE. THE RECAP
EXPLAINS HOW THE WORDS ANSWER EACH OTHER.

THERE ARE REPLIES TO LEARN BEFORE THIS CONTEST.
PRACTICE WILL TEACH THE MISSING MATERIAL,
INCLUDING ANY EARLIER LINES YOU HAVE NOT MET YET.

YOU HAVE LEARNED THIS CONTEST'S FULL REPLY POOL.
YOU CAN COMPETE, PRACTICE AGAIN OR REVIEW THE
NOTEBOOK.

THAT REPLY ANSWERS THE LINE. NO SCORE IN PRACTICE;

LINE: YOU'RE SO SLOW ON THE UPTAKE, THE ECHO
FINISHES BEFORE YOU ANSWER.
REPLY: YOUR ECHO GETS MORE PRACTICE THAN THE REST
OF US.

LINE: YOUR BIG ENTRANCE HAS THE ELEGANCE OF
TROUSERS CAUGHT IN A DRAWER.
REPLY: YOURS TAKES LONGER, AND EVERYONE STILL
WISHES YOU'D ZIP IT.

LINE: YOU WANT THE LAST WORD BEFORE YOU'VE THOUGHT
OF THE FIRST.
REPLY: YOU ONLY WANT IT SO NOBODY CAN CHECK THE
MIDDLE.

LINE: YOU'RE A REHEARSAL THAT SOMEHOW GOT AN
AUDIENCE.
REPLY: YOU'RE AN INTERVAL THAT THINKS IT'S THE
SHOW.

LINE: YOU SAY YES SO OFTEN I COULD SELL TICKETS TO
YOUR NOD.
REPLY: YOU'D SELL THE SEATS AND ASK ME TO STAND.

LINE: YOU COULDN'T FOLLOW AN ARROW WITHOUT ASKING
WHICH WAY IT POINTS.
REPLY: YOU'D PUT YOUR NAME ON IT AND CALL IT A
PARADE.

LINE: YOU HAVE THE PRESENCE OF A TABLE THAT NEEDS
CLEARING.
REPLY: THEN STOP ARRANGING YOURSELF AROUND ME.

LINE: YOUR IDEA OF AN ENTRANCE IS GETTING STUCK
SIDEWAYS.
REPLY: YOURS IS MAKING EVERYONE ELSE STAND ASIDE.

LINE: YOUR POSTURE COULD MAKE A COAT HANGER GIVE
UP.
REPLY: YOURS COULD PUT A CREASE IN SOUP.

LINE: YOU'RE WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE ROUGH SKETCH
TAKES ITSELF SERIOUSLY.
REPLY: YOU'RE WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE SIGNATURE
COVERS THE DRAWING.

LINE: YOU'D HANG A CURTAIN OVER THE DOOR AND CALL
THE ROOM FINISHED.
REPLY: YOU'D CALL THE PEOPLE STUCK OUTSIDE A
WAITING LIST.

LINE: YOU THINK GOOD TASTE IS WHATEVER FITS ON
YOUR PLATE.
REPLY: YOU THINK IT MEANS MAKING EVERYONE ASK
WHERE YOU GOT IT.

LINE: YOU MADE CARRYING A PANEL LOOK LIKE A PUBLIC
INQUIRY.
REPLY: YOU SUPPLIED THE OPENING STATEMENT.

LINE: I COULD HAVE DONE THAT WITH ONE HAND TIED
BEHIND MY BACK.
REPLY: YES, BUT THEN WHO'D POINT AT YOUR
HANDIWORK?

LINE: YOU'D ASK FOR DIRECTIONS WHILE STANDING IN
THE DOORWAY.
REPLY: YOU'D STAND THERE UNTIL SOMEONE ASKED.

LINE: YOU'RE A DEMONSTRATION OF WHY INSTRUCTIONS
HAVE PICTURES.
REPLY: YOU'RE THE REASON THE PICTURES DON'T HAVE
SOUND.

LINE: WITHOUT YOUR FRIENDS, YOU'D STILL BE WEDGED
IN THAT DOORWAY.
REPLY: AND YOU'D STILL BE TRYING TO SQUEEZE YOUR
OPINION IN BESIDE ME.

LINE: YOU THINK STANDING NEAR USEFUL PEOPLE MAKES
YOU USEFUL.
REPLY: YOU THINK STANDING IN FRONT OF THEM MAKES
YOU IN CHARGE.

LINE: SOME PEOPLE KNOW WHEN A SPEECH HAS GONE ON
LONG ENOUGH.
REPLY: SHALL I FETCH ONE?

LINE: YOU CALL THAT A TOAST? I'VE HAD WIND WITH
MORE CEREMONY.
REPLY: AT LEAST THEY KNOW WHICH END MY SPEECH IS
COMING FROM.

LINE: YOU TURN EVERY SIMPLE INSTRUCTION INTO A
DISCUSSION.
REPLY: YOURS BECOME SUGGESTIONS THE MOMENT YOU
WANT ANOTHER HELPING.

LINE: YOU'D FORGET YOUR OWN SUPPER IF NOBODY PUT
YOUR NAME ON IT.
REPLY: YOURS COULD LOSE ITS LABEL; WE'D FOLLOW THE
COMPLAINTS.

LINE: YOU COULDN'T KEEP TO THE POINT IF IT WAS
MARKED ON THE FLOOR.
REPLY: YOU'D STAND ON IT AND COMPLAIN THERE WASN'T
ROOM FOR ANYONE ELSE.

LINE: YOUR IDEA OF RESPONSIBILITY IS HANDING
SOMEONE A CLOTH.
REPLY: YOURS IS WAITING UNTIL THEY'VE FINISHED
BEFORE POINTING OUT THE DUST.
